topic: Inside DeepSeek's open agent harness: four verified designs and what builders should own
thesis: The harness layer decides whether agent work completes; DeepSeek opening DSH makes the layer readable, and the durable move for builders is copying three practices while investing in the portable asset layer.

facts.claim: The same DeepSeek V4-Flash model across eight harnesses on thirty real workflows produced success rates from 46.7% to 66.7% and about 7x cost per completed task.
facts.sensitivity: Use the spread, never the ranking; Composio itself caveats the order.

facts.claim: Armin Ronacher, co-founder of Earendil (the company behind Pi, the test's top scorer), said reading the DSH repo was the first time something new in the space made him want to revisit his own choices.
facts.sensitivity: Attribute via Earendil; Pi's original creator is Mario Zechner.

facts.claim: DeepSeek open-sourced DSH under MIT on 2026-08-13, two days after Composio's numbers, the same day V4-Pro went GA.
facts.sensitivity: Verify official announcement wording before publish (open ledger item C5).

facts.claim: DSH logs 44 session event types; exactly 3 are model-visible (user message, assistant message, tool result).
The model's context is recomputed from the append-only log before every request, and a runtime invariant refuses to send a request that mismatches the log-derived projection.
At launch-week list prices a DeepSeek cache hit cost roughly 1/50th (V4-Flash) to 1/120th (V4-Pro) of a miss.
A live-API e2e test asserts every request after a session's first reports cache-read tokens > 0; tool schemas are sorted in a fixed locale-independent order; the system prompt carries no clock.
The agent loop is one config row that disabled: true removes; the code preset is the standard preset's configuration plus one appended tool-presentation row.
facts.sensitivity: Comments differ between preset files; the identity claim is configuration-content level.

facts.claim: Two silent config crashes (one shipping with 178 green tests and 100% coverage) each produced a new pre-release static check; 27 such checks exist at the pin.
facts.sensitivity: Never phrase as 'doc-sync runs 27' (it runs 28). Claim-ledger C28.

facts.claim: 12,293 commits in 64 days by 37 named authors; top author 5,235; merge-history branch prefixes counted first-party: worktree/ 210, codex/ 209; markdown files outnumber TypeScript files.
facts.sensitivity: Narration rounds 5,235 to 'five thousand' (accepted in listening review).

facts.claim: A day-two process note states agents follow enforced gates far more reliably than prose conventions; rejected proposals are kept while their reasoning still blocks a mistake; postmortems must end in checks verified to turn red.
facts.sensitivity: Retention rule is scoped: rejected pruned when stale, superseded notes archived frozen.

facts.claim: DSH's own docs: the loop-runaway guard is advisory and eventually goes silent; the file read/write/edit tools have no timeout; early testers say daily experience trails Claude Code and Codex.
facts.sensitivity: Bash DOES have an executor timeout; the no-timeout claim is scoped to file tools.

facts.claim: Anthropic keeps its harness closed and subscription-wired; DeepSeek gives DSH away and makes it read rivals' formats — read by Aaron as moat vs token funnel.
facts.sensitivity: Labeled as Aaron's read in narration ('this is my read'); never presented as reported fact.

facts.claim: Models are rented; the harness layer churns (the repo warns compatibility will break); the portable layer every harness reads — skills, instruction files, decision records — is what builders own.
facts.sensitivity: The closing frame is authored judgment built on verified compatibility facts.
